This year has officially become the year of the "super app." OpenAI recently launched its own super app and openly admitted that the app "is a bit of a mess." Meanwhile, the Microsoft CEO has also confirmed that a Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.

Microsoft Copilot "super app" to integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other features

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot chat, coding and intelligent agent features. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on the company's earnings call on Wednesday that the app will be launched this year, covering "consumer and business experiences." Nadella pointed out: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork and even Autopilots. This quarter, we will integrate various Copilot experiences, including coding, into one single super app... This is a major step, and I look forward to sharing more details with everyone later."

The process of OpenAI launching its own "super app" has turned into a disaster. But that obviously hasn't deterred other companies from following this super app route.

Perhaps Microsoft can better deliver an all-in-one app and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella has also recently stated that the company is shifting its focus from apps to intelligent agents. The AI era is still in its infancy, and the trends and best practices for building AI-driven interfaces are still constantly evolving.

As for Apple, there are no signs of it moving toward a super app; instead, it continues to launch independent and specialised new apps. It remains to be seen whether this strategy will change in the future.

What are your thoughts on the recent "super app" craze? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
